GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/interval.js so that `Interval.fromISO` works correctly when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true. A hidden test named "Interval.fromISO works with Settings.throwOnInvalid" must pass. The bug: `Interval.fromISO(text, opts)` calls `DateTime.fromISO(s, opts)` / `DateTime.fromISO(e, opts)` and `Duration.fromISO(...)` directly. When `Settings.throwOnInvalid === true`, those calls THROW (InvalidDateTimeError / InvalidDurationError) instead of returning an invalid instance, so `Interval.fromISO("2016-05-25/PT1H")` (start/duration form) or `Interval.fromISO("PT1H/2016-05-25")` (duration/end form) throws even though it should return a valid Interval. Also `Interval.fromISO("garbage")` should throw InvalidIntervalError (that part is expected).

REQUIRED FIX APPROACH (mirror upstream): in `static fromISO(text, opts)`, parse the start and end DateTimes inside try/catch blocks, recording `startIsValid`/`endIsValid` booleans, then use those booleans for the control flow instead of `start.isValid`/`end.isValid`. Keep the existing final `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)` return. Make sure the duration branch also behaves sanely when throwOnInvalid is true (e.g. wrap the `Duration.fromISO` calls in try/catch too, or otherwise ensure a non-parsable duration does not throw an unexpected error type; prefer the minimal change that keeps `Interval.fromISO` returning/behaving correctly).

Delete the temp file afterwards.
4. Also run eslint if configured: `cd /luxon && npx eslint src/interval.js`.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js so that a hidden test named "DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February" passes. Only /luxon/src/impl/util.js may be modified. Do NOT modify or delete any test file, and do not reformat unrelated code.

DIAGNOSIS (already established, verify it yourself): `objToLocalTS(obj)` in /luxon/src/impl/util.js builds `Date.UTC(obj.year, obj.month-1, obj.day, ...)` and, for years 0..99, undoes JS's 19XX interpretation with `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`. That is wrong when `obj.day` overflows the month (e.g. day=92 for December): the day overflow is first resolved in the 19XX/20XX calendar (where February can have 29 days, e.g. year 2000 is a leap year) and only then is the year changed, so the result can be off by a day when the target year's February has a different number of days (e.g. year 100 is not a leap year). Example: DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 }) should be 0100-03-02 but currently comes out as 0100-03-01.

REQUIRED FIX: in `objToLocalTS`, inside the `if (obj.year < 100 && obj.year >= 0)` branch, replace the year-only adjustment with one that re-applies the month and day so the overflow is recomputed in the correct calendar, i.e.:

    d = new Date(d);
    // set the month and day again, this is necessary because year 2000 is a leap year, but year 100 is not
    d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day);

(keep `let d = Date.UTC(...)` and `return +d;` as they are).
